title: WPSB/562/2026 of SUMIT SAXENA Vs UNION BANK OF INDIA

HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
THE HON'BLE CHIEF JUSTICE MR. MANOJ KUMAR GUPTA
AND
THE HON'BLE JUSTICE MR. SIDDHARTHA SAH
Writ Petition (S/B) No.562 of 2026
Sumit Saxena --Petitioner
Versus
Union Bank of India & Others --Respondents
August 25, 2026
----------------------------------------------------------------------
Presence:-
Mr. Milan Laskar, learned counsel for the petitioner appeared through V.C.
Mr. Vikas Kumar Guglani, learned counsel for the respondent-Bank appeared
through V.C.
----------------------------------------------------------------------
JUDGMENT : (per Mr. Manoj Kumar Gupta, C.J.)
1. The present writ petition has been filed
challenging the transfer order dated 28.04.2026 passed
by the respondent-Bank, whereby the petitioner, who
was serving as Senior Manager (BRM) at Haldwani,
District Nainital, Uttarakhand, has been transferred to
Zonal Office, Bhopal, Madhya Pradesh.
2. The petitioner filed a departmental appeal
against the transfer order and the ground taken in the
appeal was that his spouse was suffering from chronic
Orthopedic psoriasis with thyroid disease and her
treatment was stated to be going on in Matrix Hospital,
Haldwani. The other ground was that his son was
1

studying in 11th standard in Haldwani. The appeal of the
petitioner was duly considered by the Departmental
Committee and it rejected the same. The petitioner has
already joined at Bhopal. The present writ petition has
been filed in the month of August 2026 after the
petitioner had joined at Bhopal.
3. Learned counsel for the petitioner has raised a
new ground for challenging the transfer order. He
submits that according to the transfer policy of the Bank,
an officer cannot be transferred to another zone within
five years. He further submits that the petitioner was
posted in the present zone only 1 year back and,
therefore, the transfer order is illegal.
4. When learned counsel for the petitioner was
queried by the Court as regards the details of postings of
the petitioner during last five years, he is unable to point
out to any such details in the writ petition. On the other
hand, learned counsel for the respondent-Bank states
that the petitioner had remained posted at Haldwani
from 01.08.2020 in different capacities and the
contention that he had been transferred to a different
zone without completing the prescribed minimum period
of posting at Haldwani zone is apparently incorrect.

5. As the aforesaid ground was not taken by the
petitioner in his representation, nor the factual
foundation in respect thereof has been laid down in the
writ petition, the same cannot be accepted.
6. Thus, we find no ground to interfere with the
transfer order. The writ petition lacks merit and is
accordingly dismissed.
(MANOJ KUMAR GUPTA, C. J.)
(SIDDHARTHA SAH, J.)
Dated : 25.08.2026
Akash
